title: Master Daochuo: Even If One Has Created Evil All One’s Life, Ten Uninterrupted Recitations at the End of Life Bring Rebirth
author: Zhanran
excerpt: On how one can be reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, Master Daochuo teaches (see in detail Master Daochuo’s Pure Land Teachings):

blocks.text: Even If One Has Created Evil All One’s Life, Ten Uninterrupted Recitations at the End of Life Bring Rebirth

inline.s: On how one can be reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, Master Daochuo teaches (see in detail
Master Daochuo’s Pure Land Teachings
If there are sentient beings who, even if they have created evil all their lives,
at the end of life, with ten uninterrupted recitations
, call my name,
and should they not be reborn, I will not attain perfect enlightenment.
[Ten uninterrupted recitations]
ten recitations without any admixture of deluded thought. Master Tanluan teaches:
With no other mind intermingled, each thought following upon the next
(in succession)
, up to ten recitations, is called ten uninterrupted recitations.”
(See in detail
Master Tanluan’s Pure Land Teachings
Question: The teaching above says:

“If there are sentient beings who, even if they have created evil all their lives, at the end of life, with ten uninterrupted recitations, call my name, and should they not be reborn, I will not attain perfect enlightenment.”

Since “even if one has created evil all one’s life,” so long as “at the end of life one has ten uninterrupted recitations” one will certainly be reborn, does that mean those who recite the Buddha’s name need not cut off evil and practice good? Is that so?
Answer:
“Even if one has created evil all one’s life, so long as at the end of life one has ten uninterrupted recitations, one will certainly be reborn”

— this shows that right mindfulness at the end of life (ten uninterrupted recitations) is of the utmost importance. That is to say: ten uninterrupted recitations at the end of life are the sole requirement for rebirth; so long as one has ten uninterrupted recitations at the end of life, one can move Amitābha Buddha to come and receive one.

But to meet this requirement, one must in ordinary times make ten uninterrupted recitations second nature through repeated practice, and cutting off evil and practicing good is a very important auxiliary condition. Therefore Master Shandao teaches:
“May all people think well upon this: whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down,
one must steel the mind and restrain oneself,

never ceasing by day or night. When the previous thought ends one’s life, the very next thought brings rebirth. To enjoy forever the effortless joy of the Dharma, and even attain Buddhahood — how delightful!”

The “steel the mind and restrain oneself” in this teaching means rousing oneself and disciplining oneself. A person who indulges himself in doing evil cannot “steel the mind and restrain oneself,” and is not in accord with single-minded Buddha-recitation free from admixture of deluded thought.
[Second nature through repeated practice] Through repeated practice, one makes ten uninterrupted recitations instinctive.
On this, Ciyun Chanzhu teaches:

“When the mind is thus bound to the Buddha, it naturally and spontaneously shields off all evil thoughts of itself. Even if one wished to do evil, because one remembers the Buddha, the evil cannot be accomplished.”
The Two Gates of Resolving Doubts and Practicing Vows for Rebirth in the Pure Land

Therefore, a person who does not steel the mind and restrain himself will find it very hard to make ten uninterrupted recitations second nature, and so his ten uninterrupted recitations at the end of life are not assured. Conversely, if one has truly made ten uninterrupted recitations second nature, one will not go on creating evil, because
“even if one wished to do evil, because one remembers the Buddha, the evil cannot be accomplished”

Although there are extremely rare exceptions, in which a person who has created evil all his life manages to achieve “ten uninterrupted recitations at the end of life”: these cases are practitioners who in a former life already possessed considerable spiritual power, but who, having not yet cut off the delusions of views and thoughts, have wandered in rebirth down to this life. In this life they have again gone astray and spent their lives creating evil. At the end of life, under the guidance of a good friend, they suddenly awaken, repent with utmost sincerity, and achieve ten uninterrupted recitations and so attain rebirth. Just consider:
were it not grounded in the bodhi-mind and deep spiritual power of a former life,
how, amid the many pains pressing together at the end of life, could one suddenly give rise to faith and vows and abruptly achieve ten uninterrupted recitations?

Therefore one must on no account imitate this, for such cases are hardly one in ten thousand among those who attain rebirth. Just consider: if in ordinary times one lets one’s conduct run loose, indulging the mind in evil, and whenever adverse or favorable circumstances appear one’s mind is carried away by them, then how, amid the many pains pressing together at the end of life, can one achieve ten uninterrupted recitations? On this principle, the patriarchs and great masters from ancient times down to the present have offered very many teachings and discussions.
For example,
Master Ouyi
says
“When the sutra says that those who have committed the ten evils and the five rebellious acts may attain rebirth,
they must in the past have planted seeds of bodhi
. If they had no seeds of bodhi, how could they meet a good friend? Even if they met a good friend who urged them on, how could they suddenly give rise to faith and vows and call the great name?”
(Lingfeng’s Collected Writings · A General Discourse at the Tianma Cloister of Shepu)
Master Ouyi also says:
Now, ten recitations at the end of life
must be deeply rooted in planted goodness
. If even now, when adverse and favorable circumstances arise, one no longer has right mindfulness
(the mind of Buddha-recitation free from admixture of deluded thought)

, how much less at the end of life? Moreover, when the pains of the end appear, one relies solely on a good friend’s encouragement; yet now, in broad daylight, one still cannot faithfully accept and practice the true maxims of a clear-sighted teacher and good friend!”
(Lingfeng’s Collected Writings
Preface to the Society for Cultivating the Pure Land Repentance and Releasing Living Beings)

Translation: To achieve the ten uninterrupted recitations at the end of life, one must deeply plant roots of goodness. If even now, whenever adverse or favorable circumstances come, one no longer has right mindfulness
(the mind of Buddha-recitation free from admixture of deluded thought)

, how much less can one maintain right mindfulness at the end of life? Moreover, if now, in broad and open daylight, one still cannot faithfully accept and practice the sincere exhortations and teachings of a clear-sighted teacher and good friend, can one vainly hope that, when the pains of the end appear, one will be able to accept and practice them merely by relying on a good friend’s reminder and guidance?
